name: Clavipectoral fascia
function: Envelops subclavius and pectoralis minor; pierced by the cephalic vein, thoracoacromial vessels, and lateral pectoral nerve; continuous inferiorly with the axillary fascia (suspensory ligament of the axilla).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Pectoral fascia
function: Thin fascia enveloping pectoralis major, continuous with the fascia of the arm/axilla.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Deltoid fascia
function: Dense fascia over deltoid, continuous distally with the brachial fascia; septa between the deltoid's multipennate segments blend with this sheet (Stecco: deltoid fascia contributes force-transmission pathways between segments).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Infraspinous fascia
function: Dense fascia roofing the infraspinous fossa, itself part of the origin surface for infraspinatus deep fibers.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Axillary fascia

bony_attachments.landmark: via continuity with the clavipectoral fascia (suspensory ligament of the axilla) -- axillary fascia itself has no direct bony insertion, it is a soft-tissue floor suspended between the pectoral and latissimus dorsi/teres major fascial margins

function: Floor of the axilla; suspended from the clavipectoral fascia (suspensory ligament of the axilla, Gerdy's ligament).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Brachial (deep) fascia of the arm

bony_attachments.landmark: via continuity with deltoid fascia proximally

function: Tubular deep fascia of the arm; sends the medial and lateral intermuscular septa inward to the humerus, dividing the arm into anterior (flexor) and posterior (extensor) osteofascial compartments.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Medial intermuscular septum of the arm
function: Separates the anterior (biceps/brachialis, musculocutaneous n.) from the posterior (triceps, radial n.) arm compartment medially; the ulnar nerve pierces it ~8cm above the elbow to enter the posterior compartment before passing behind the medial epicondyle.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Lateral intermuscular septum of the arm
function: Separates the anterior from the posterior arm compartment laterally; the radial nerve pierces it (traveling from posterior to anterior compartment) approximately at the junction of the middle and distal thirds of the arm.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Antebrachial (deep) fascia of the forearm
compartment_contents: all forearm flexor and extensor muscle groups
function: Tubular deep fascia of the forearm, thickened distally into the flexor and extensor retinacula; gives origin to some superficial forearm muscle fibers (e.g. FDS, FCU) directly from its deep surface.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Interosseous membrane (forearm)
compartment_contents: divides the forearm into volar and dorsal osteofascial compartments together with the antebrachial fascia
function: Fibrous sheet linking radius and ulna along their shafts; transmits load from radius to ulna at the wrist, gives origin to deep flexor/extensor fibers (FPL, FDP, EPL, EI), and its central band remains taut through the pronation-supination range (functions as the forearm's primary load-transfer + rotational-stability structure).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Volar (flexor) osteofascial compartment of the forearm
function: Bounded by the antebrachial fascia (superficial), radius/ulna + interosseous membrane (deep); further divided into superficial/intermediate/deep layers (Gray's classic 4-layer scheme). Elevated pressure here (e.g. after fracture) causes volar (Volkmann's) compartment syndrome.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Dorsal (extensor) osteofascial compartment of the forearm
function: Bounded by the antebrachial fascia (superficial), radius/ulna + interosseous membrane (deep, shared with the volar compartment).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Mobile wad (Henry's mobile wad)
function: Lateral muscle group, radial-nerve-innervated but functionally/fascially distinct from the main dorsal extensor mass; important surgical landmark for the anterior (Henry) approach to the radius.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Flexor retinaculum (transverse carpal ligament)

bony_attachments.landmark: scaphoid tubercle + trapezium tubercle (radial attachments); pisiform + hook of hamate (ulnar attachments)

compartment_contents: median_n (passes through the carpal tunnel deep to the retinaculum)
function: Roofs the carpal tunnel; thenar and hypothenar muscles originate from its palmar surface. Ulnar nerve and artery pass superficial to it (through Guyon's canal, not the carpal tunnel). Compression here causes carpal tunnel syndrome (median n.).
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Extensor retinaculum (dorsal carpal ligament)
compartment_contents: 6 septated compartments: (1) APL+EPB, (2) ECRL+ECRB, (3) EPL, (4) extensor_digitorum_r + extensor indicis, (5) extensor digiti minimi, (6) extensor_carpi_ulnaris_r
function: Sends septa down to the underlying radius/ulna/carpal bones creating 6 discrete fibro-osseous tunnels (a textbook example of retinacular osteofascial compartmentalization), each with its own synovial sheath, preventing bowstringing of the extensor tendons during wrist extension.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Palmar aponeurosis

bony_attachments.landmark: continuous proximally with the flexor retinaculum / palmaris longus tendon

function: Thick triangular fascia deep to palmar skin, protecting the underlying tendons/nerves/vessels; gives off 4 longitudinal digital bands that blend into the fibrous flexor sheaths, and vertical septa that create the palmar fascial (mid-palmar, thenar, hypothenar) spaces relevant to the spread of palmar infections.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Fibrous flexor sheaths (annular + cruciate pulleys A1-A5, C1-C3)

bony_attachments.landmark: palmar surface of each phalanx and the palmar plates of the MCP/PIP joints

function: Osteofibrous tunnels overlying each finger's flexor tendons; the 5 annular (A1-A5) pulleys (over the phalanges/joints) keep the tendons apposed to bone (preventing bowstringing during flexion, which is essential for efficient joint torque), while the 3 thinner cruciate (C1-C3) pulleys collapse to allow the sheath to fold during flexion. A2 and A4 are the biomechanically most critical (over mid-shaft of proximal and middle phalanges); their rupture ('climber's finger') causes clinically visible tendon bowstringing.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell) ch.7; Stecco C, Functional Atlas of the Human Fascial System (2015), Churchill Livingstone -- upper limb fascial continuity chapters; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Bicipital aponeurosis (lacertus fibrosus)

bony_attachments.landmark: blends with the antebrachial fascia over the flexor mass

function: A flat expansion from the distal biceps tendon fanning medially over the cubital fossa. It roofs the brachial artery and median nerve, protecting them during venepuncture at the median cubital vein, and it is the structure that must be released in distal biceps repair. Also a recognised site of median nerve compression.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Cubital tunnel retinaculum (Osborne's ligament)
function: Roofs the cubital tunnel between the two heads of flexor carpi ulnaris. It tightens in elbow flexion, which is why cubital tunnel syndrome symptoms are worse with a flexed elbow and why night splinting in extension helps.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Arcade of Struthers

bony_attachments.landmark: medial intermuscular septum, about 8 cm proximal to the medial epicondyle

function: A fascial band from the medial head of triceps to the medial intermuscular septum. A proximal site of ulnar nerve compression, and the reason an anterior transposition must release it or the nerve simply kinks at a new level. Distinct from the ligament of Struthers, a separate and rarer bony spur structure involving the median nerve.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Arcade of Frohse

bony_attachments.landmark: proximal fibrous margin of the supinator's superficial head

function: The tendinous proximal edge of supinator through which the posterior interosseous nerve passes. The commonest site of posterior interosseous nerve entrapment, producing finger-drop with preserved wrist extension and no sensory loss -- which is what separates it from a radial nerve palsy.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Guyon's canal (ulnar tunnel)

bony_attachments.landmark: pisiform medially and hook of hamate laterally

function: Roofed by the palmar carpal ligament and floored by the flexor retinaculum. Because it lies SUPERFICIAL to the flexor retinaculum, carpal tunnel release does not decompress it. Compression here spares the dorsal cutaneous branch, which leaves the nerve proximal to the wrist -- the clinical test that localises the lesion.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Quadrangular space
function: Bounded by teres minor above, teres major below, the long head of triceps medially and the humerus laterally. Quadrangular space syndrome compresses the axillary nerve here, giving deltoid weakness and numbness over the regimental badge area.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)

name: Triangular interval
function: Bounded by teres major above, the long head of triceps medially and the humeral shaft laterally. The radial nerve passes through it into the posterior compartment, which is why a mid-shaft humeral fracture threatens the nerve.
source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.; Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998)
